clue.text: Short dating description: 'wearing thongs (not northern model)'

indicators.note: wearing in the sense of worn out or frayed tells us the letters of thongs are reshuffled
not tells us some letters of thongs are left out before the reshuffle

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts advertiser describes themself in tiny underwear, with a disclaimer about not being a northern model.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and T out of THONGS to leave HOGS, then rearrange those letters. GSOH is lonely-hearts shorthand for 'good sense of humour'.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal ads abbreviate 'good sense of humour' to four initials, the classic boast in a lonely-hearts column.

clue.text: King, say, eating good eggs up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so the whole is reversed
eating means the first pieces take the next one inside them

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for 'for example', which say can mean
roe is fish eggs

explanation.surface: A monarch is pictured breakfasting on eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: EG and G make EGG, which 'eating' wraps round ROE to give EGROEG; 'up' then reverses it. The comma means 'King, say' reads as 'for example, a king', but say is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: George is the name of six British monarchs, so it is a fair example of a king's name.

clue.text: Earl employed to cover up one showing signs of old age?

parts.note: Earl Grey, the British prime minister and the tea, gives GREY

indicators.note: to cover up means the word for employed hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: employed means hired
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A nobleman takes a job concealing someone who is visibly ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turning grey is the commonest outward sign of getting older, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Inside, check new oil colour

indicators.note: Inside, placed at the front, tells us one piece goes within another

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: new means the letters of oil are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A mechanic looks inside an engine to check its fresh oil's colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OIL to IOL, and 'Inside' puts that within VET.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a bluish-purple shade, one of the colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Hypothetical argument about skills with worker

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for skills is read backwards

parts.note: arts are skills, as in the arts of war
a man is a worker, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A debate about craft skills and labourers, conducted purely in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ARTS to give STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw man is a weak version of an opponent's case, invented so that it can be knocked down easily.

clue.text: Setter's embracing a royal queen

indicators.note: embracing means holding the following letters within

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says my, so setter's gives MY

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler hugs a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary has been the name of several queens, among them Mary, Queen of Scots, and Mary I.

clue.text: Attractive motor, no boot, silver interior: £1,000

indicators.note: interior means silver goes within the shortened word
no boot means the last letter, the back end where a car's boot is, is removed

parts.note: a motor is an engine
AG is the chemical symbol for silver
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A car advert: attractive engine, no boot, silver interior, a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no boot' cuts ENGINE to ENGIN, and 'interior' puts AG inside it to make ENGAGIN. The boot is a car's trunk, at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming, the quality of drawing people in.

clue.text: County furniture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire, an English county north of London, is written Beds for short.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is both a county's abbreviated name and the plural of a bedroom item.

clue.text: Small fruit with perfect flavour

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
mint means perfect, as in mint condition

explanation.surface: A little fruit with a wonderful taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a herb whose taste is used in chewing gum and toothpaste.

clue.text: Key notes? That's musical

parts.note: A is a musical key
N is an abbreviation for note, so two of them give NN
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these are key notes and is told that's musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the Broadway show about a little orphan girl, famous for the song Tomorrow.

clue.text: After temperature rises, bear becomes badger

indicators.note: as on a tap, cold turns to hot when the temperature rises, so C is swapped for H

parts.note: to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A bear warms up and turns into a badger, as if by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Both bear and badger look like animals, but each is a verb here: bear is carry, and badger is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry and to badger both mean to pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Perhaps 2000 or 2020 players struggle to control Real's midfield

indicators.note: to control means to hold, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece
struggle suggests the players being tossed about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the middle two letters of Real, as in Real Madrid

explanation.surface: Footballers battle to dominate Real Madrid's midfield in two particular seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAYERS is rearranged to LPYEARS with EA held after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 2000 and 2020 had 29 days in February, which makes them examples of years with an extra day.

clue.text: Racing driver, rock singer and holy man drink sparkling water

parts.note: ST is short for saint

indicators.note: sparkling suggests the letters of water fizzing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of famous people, then a holy man ordering fizzy water.
explanation.walkthrough: Jackie Stewart was a Formula One champion and Rod Stewart a rock singer; in this puzzle's theme the name also belongs to James Stewart, star of It's a Wonderful Life.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by the motor-racing champion Jackie and the rock star Rod.

clue.text: Stories of elite soldiers capturing a German leader

indicators.note: capturing means the soldiers hold the next letters inside

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's elite special forces regiment

indicators.note: a German leader here is the first letter of German

explanation.surface: Tales of special forces seizing a German commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long narratives, originally the Norse tales of heroes.

clue.text: Mother's tough dog

parts.note: ma is mother; the 's stands for is, joining her to the next word
stiff means tough, as in stiff competition

explanation.surface: Mum's hound is a hardy beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a big, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Kraken eats men! So scary, right?

indicators.note: scary hints at the letters being frightened into disorder

explanation.surface: A horror-story claim that the kraken devours people, with a nervous 'right?' at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: EATS, MEN and SO are rearranged together to give SEAMONSTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a giant monster of Scandinavian legend said to drag ships under the waves.

clue.text: Around capitals for students learning lots (and field trips)

indicators.note: Around means the string of letters is turned round, read from the end
capitals for means the initial letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A comment that students learn a great deal on field trips.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of students, learning, lots, and, field give SLLAF, and 'Around' turns that backwards. 'field trips' looks like a phrase but trips is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Falls and trips are both stumbles; the plural verb 'trips' matches 'falls' too.

clue.text: Attempt extremely wide yorker at the end to batsman

parts.note: a go is an attempt

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of wide
at the end means the final letter of yorker

explanation.surface: A bowler tries a very wide yorker, a ball pitched at the batsman's feet, at the end of the over.
explanation.walkthrough: David Gower was an elegant England cricket captain of the 1980s; a yorker is a delivery aimed at the batsman's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: David Gower was a celebrated left-handed England batsman and captain.

parts.note: the clue has no words at all, only an ellipsis and a question mark, so it describes itself

explanation.walkthrough: The clue itself contains no words, so the answer describes the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no words at all is silent or speechless, exactly what this clue is.

clue.text: Managed to uncover Sinatra?

indicators.note: to uncover means to strip off the covering, the first and last letters

parts.note: Frank Sinatra, the singer

explanation.surface: An attempt to expose Frank Sinatra.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something is to manage it, so ran means managed.

clue.text: Made good wine, drinking up another takes time

indicators.note: drinking means the red wine takes the following in

parts.note: red is a wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece reads from bottom to top
takes means the second wine takes in the letter for time

parts.note: another wine, after red, is rosé

explanation.surface: A decent wine is drunk alongside another, which takes a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another wine: ROSE 'takes' T to give ROTSE, 'up' reverses it to ESTOR, and RED is 'drinking' that.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore is to repair or return to former condition, which is what made good means.

clue.text: Guardian article by setter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
gel sets, as a hair product does

explanation.surface: A Guardian newspaper piece written by the crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the newspaper but means a guardian angel, and setter is not the compiler but something that sets, hair gel.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel watches over a person; in this theme, Clarence is George Bailey's guardian angel.

clue.text: Son attempts to steal 500 Australian trousers

indicators.note: to steal means to take in, so the attempts hold the next letter

parts.note: tries are attempts
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A boy tries to pinch five hundred pairs of Aussie trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Strides is informal, especially Australian, slang for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang trousers are called strides, after the long steps legs take.

clue.text: God to regularly hoover vehicle after parking

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the parking letter

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the first, third and fifth

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A deity is told to vacuum the car after parking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes HOE from hoover, and 'after parking' puts these after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebus, the bright one, is an epithet of Apollo, the Greek sun god.

clue.text: Perhaps 11p fur?

parts.note: the letter P as written
otter is a fur, from the animal's pelt

explanation.surface: A cryptic question whether 11 might be a penny's worth of fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is HARRY, the answer at 11 across, and Harry Potter is the boy wizard. Potter is also the villain of It's a Wonderful Life, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is J.K. Rowling's boy wizard, so the surname completes the name at 11.

clue.text: Court jester?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a castle's courtyard, and the Old ... is London's criminal court
second meaning: Bill ... is a British comedian, a modern jester

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court jester' reads as the king's fool, but it splits in two. Bill Bailey is a British stand-up comic; the question mark admits a comedian is only loosely a jester.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailey names both a castle's walled courtyard and a well-known comedian, Bill Bailey.

clue.text: Connolly, try a bit of toast and butter

parts.note: Billy Connolly is the Scottish comedian
to have a go is to try

indicators.note: a bit of means the first letter of toast

explanation.surface: Someone urges Billy Connolly to sample a morsel of toast and butter.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter is not the spread but one who butts, as a billy goat does with its horns.
explanation.definitionFit: A male goat charges with its head, which makes it a creature that butts.

clue.text: Ring inventor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ring is what a ... does, and a ring on the phone is a ...
second meaning: Alexander Graham ... invented the telephone

explanation.walkthrough: Ring is a noun for a phone call, as in 'give me a bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a phone call is a bell, and the telephone's inventor was Alexander Graham Bell.

clue.text: Young people today go to Magaluf at last

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Today's youngsters head to Magaluf, the Majorcan party resort, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Magaluf is a Spanish resort famous for young British holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is jokey British slang for youth culture, mimicking a London pronunciation of youth.

clue.text: Tin provided strong smell

parts.note: SN is the chemical symbol for tin
if means provided, as in provided that
F is forte, the musical abbreviation for strong or loud

explanation.surface: A can gives off a powerful odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniff is a short smell taken through the nose.

clue.text: Car made in four dimensions, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the letters are what is heard spoken

parts.note: four dimensions is four Ds, D being short for dimension

explanation.surface: A car built in four dimensions, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: D stands for dimension, as in 3D, so four dimensions reads as 'four D'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford is a car manufacturer, so a Ford is a make of car.

clue.text: State dollars get old rope

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Louisiana
the dollar sign is an S with a stroke, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: A cowboy state's dollars buy an old rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose, used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Watch the Queen on tele, surprisingly a tool for making holes

parts.note: to eye is to watch

indicators.note: surprisingly means the letters of tele turn out in an unexpected order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Watching the Queen on television, surprisingly, shows a hole-punching tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Tele is short for television; it is rearranged to LETE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeleteer is a pointed instrument like a bodkin, used for punching small holes for laces or eyelets.
